title: Solve the model and read its answer

blocks.text: A harbor authority keeps its quay repairs in a list of `Project` records: a cost, a value (both in $k) and a `must_do` flag for repairs an inspector has ordered. Its analysts want one function that builds the selection model, solves it and hands back an answer they can trust, including the day the budget cannot even cover the ordered repairs.
Write `solve_plan(projects, budget)` in `solve.py`. It builds and solves this model with HiGHS, with $`P`$ the projects, $`M \subseteq P`$ the must-do ones and $`B`$ the budget:

It returns a tuple `(status, value, plan)`. `status` is the name of the solve's termination reason (`"OPTIMAL"`, `"INFEASIBLE"`, ...). When the status is `OPTIMAL`, `value` is the objective value and `plan` the frozenset of funded project ids; otherwise both are `None`, because a solve that found no plan has no value to report.
About fifteen lines: the five parts of the lesson's program, in order.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    cost: int
    value: int
    must_do: bool = False


def solve_plan(projects: list[Project], budget: int) -> tuple[str, float | None, frozenset[str] | None]:
    """Build the selection model, solve it with HiGHS, and read the answer status first."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="selection")
    x = {p.pid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}") for p in projects}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(p.cost * x[p.pid] for p in projects) <= budget, name="budget")
    for p in projects:
        if p.must_do:
            model.add_linear_constraint(x[p.pid] == 1, name=f"must_{p.pid}")
    model.maximize(sum(p.value * x[p.pid] for p in projects))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    status = result.termination.reason.name
    if result.termination.reason != mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL:
        return status, None, None
    plan = frozenset(pid for pid, var in x.items() if result.variable_values(var) > 0.5)
    return status, result.objective_value(), plan


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo = [Project("A", 50, 80, must_do=True), Project("B", 30, 40), Project("C", 20, 35)]
    print(solve_plan(demo, 90))
    print(solve_plan(demo, 40))

cases.says: an allowed budget returns status OPTIMAL, the best value and the plan
a budget no plan fits returns INFEASIBLE with no value and no plan, not an empty plan worth 0
the must-do project is in the plan though leaving it out would be worth more
the value is the sum of whole projects, so the variables are binary rather than fractions

origin.section: Every MathOpt Program Has the Same Five Parts

concepts: is_integer turns the LP's fractions into whole projects, which is what makes the model a MILP
a MathOpt program is a model, variables with their domains, named rows, one objective and a solve
a solve's status is read before its values, and INFEASIBLE means no plan satisfies every rule
